ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider (as Ryde voucher per NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde for review of the false "I'm Here" arrival confirmation + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case: the driver cancelled and claims a rider no-show, so it is examined under NS-1/NS-2 [F3]. The cancellation fee of $6.61 was charged on that basis [F6].

NS-1 requires all three elements. Element (i) is met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 [F5]. Element (ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 1000 m from the pickup point, and the closest approach in the whole trip was 873 m, never within 200 m [F5][F1]. Element (iii) also fails: after the tap the driver stayed inside the 200 m radius for 0 s, against the required >180 s [F5]; the driver's "more than 3 minutes" claim rests only on his own message and post-trip statement [F10][F12], which cannot override the GPS record of a stationary wait 1000 m away [F2].

Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) are not satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 is refunded in full [F6][NS-2]. The rider's account of waiting at the pickup point and seeing no car [F9] is consistent with the trace, and the driver's message "Reached already" [F8] is contradicted by the system record [F1][F5]. The trace separately marks the arrival confirmation as a false one (tap while not at pickup), which calls for flag_account under NS-2 and RD-6-style account review [F5][F1][NS-2]; the driver profile (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d) supports the account action but does not decide the case [F17]. Amount: the charged cancellation fee is $6.61 [F6], refunded in full; no distance-based computation applies because this is a cancellation-fee dispute, not a route-deviation one.

The $6.61 is a cancellation fee, so it is disputed within NS-0/NS-7 and refunded in voucher form [F3][NS-7].
